ai.overview: The Washington Commanders put their Belt Holders lineal championship on the line for the first time in this reign when they host the surging Cincinnati Bengals on November 23, 2026. Washington sits at 3-5-1 after a narrow 24-21 win at the Giants, while Cincinnati arrives red-hot with four straight victories and a 6-2 record. This marks the first time these franchises have ever met with the belt at stake.
key_matchups: Cincinnati's four-game winning streak and high-powered offense (43-36, 35-13, 31-24 in recent wins) against a Washington defense that allowed 20 to the Rams in their last home loss
Washington's 3-5-1 record and inconsistent form (including a 27-27 tie) versus Cincinnati's 6-2 mark and momentum from a 34-17 road win at Atlanta
The all-time series sits nearly even at 6-5-1 in Washington's favor, with the Commanders winning the last meeting 38-33 in 2024
ai.betting_angles: The Elo model calls this a toss-up despite Cincinnati's superior record and current form. The Bengals have won four straight games, posting at least 31 points in each victory, while Washington has alternated results and sits well below .500 at 3-5-1. However, Washington did win the last meeting 38-33 in 2024 and holds a slight edge in the all-time series.
ai.prediction_writeup: Cincinnati's four-game winning streak and offensive firepower—scoring 34, 43, 35, and 31 points in those victories—should prove too much for a Washington squad that's struggled to consistency at 3-5-1. While the Commanders won the 2024 meeting 38-33 and the Elo model sees a toss-up, the momentum gap is significant. Washington has won just once in their last five and needed a three-point margin against the struggling Giants. The Bengals' 6-2 record reflects a team hitting its stride, and they'll claim the belt in their first-ever championship matchup with Washington.
